answer: A bond of 17% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. Deposits are visible in reef, and timber reconciles the forfeits at each close. Because the custody account is separate, someone cannot recycle one pool of capital across 88 aliases, and each one needs its own funded anchor account. Each duplicate costs another 192 dollars in locked collateral and another 9 days of waiting. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
